title: Saffron Tech streaming p95 & concurrency readiness review
summary: Discovery call focused on p95 latency targets for streaming and non-streaming inference, expected concurrency, and token/sec benchmarking. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) with security constraints (SSO/KMS, SOC2). Agreed to run a 48-hour perf pilot using Redwood perf template; Redwood to share pricing matrix and security pack.
next_steps: Maya to send dedicated vs hosted cost matrix and perf-run template by 2026-05-29
Set up perf pilot (48h) and test account - Redwood/Marco to coordinate scheduling
Redwood to provide SOC2/ISO docs and KMS integration guide
Schedule follow-up to review pilot results week of 2026-06-08
action_items: Maya Chen - Send pricing matrix, perf-run template and onboarding checklist - 2026-05-29
Liam O'Neill - Prepare quick-start perf harness and example configs for 1xA100/4xA100 profiles - 2026-05-30
Marco Ruiz (Saffron) - Provision test VPC peering and share network details - 2026-06-01
Daniel Kim (Saffron) - Provide representative prompt sets and target p95 scenarios - 2026-05-29
header:
Date: 2026-05-27 | Start: 16:00 PDT | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (CTO - Saffron), Marco Ruiz (Infra), Daniel Kim (ML), Aisha Patel (Product)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE. With me is Liam, our SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Priya Shah: Doing well, thanks. Busy week, so appreciate you fitting us in.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Absolutely, we wanted to focus today on your p95 targets for streaming and non-streaming text gen, expected concurrency, and then agree a path for a short perf pilot.
[00:28] Marco Ruiz: Quick context: we run a conversational assistant in-prod, about 120k MAU, peak bursts during support windows. We're seeing tail latency spikes. Our product target is p95 < 250ms for streaming responses end-to-end.
[00:42] Liam O'Neill: Okay, that's helpful. Is that 250ms including network hop to client or just server-side generation?
[00:49] Marco Ruiz: That's end-to-end from client send to first token streamed. So network included.
[00:55] Maya Chen: Good to clarify. For sizing, we usually separate network/WAF and server token generation. Redwood can aim for p95 gen under 150-180ms for the models you mentioned, leaving room for network.
[01:08] Daniel Kim: The models we're testing are an MPT-like 11B variant and a dense 33B. We also are exploring quantized variants to reduce cost.
[01:18] Liam O'Neill: Got it. For streaming, the per-token latency matters more — the initial prefill and then steady-state tokens/sec. What's your desired steady-state throughput (tokens/sec) per stream?
[01:29] Priya Shah: Ideally 250-400 tokens/sec when generating summaries and follow-ups. For some longer responses we can accept lower throughput but p95 must hold.
[01:38] Maya Chen: Ok, so aiming for 250-400 steady-state. With an 11B quantized model on a modern A100 or H100 profile we commonly hit ~300-450 tokens/sec per GPU in steady state depending on sequence length and KV cache hit rate. For 33B it drops.
[01:55] Marco Ruiz: What's the KV cache behavior here? We talked about prefix caching in the doc but not sure how it maps to our multi-tenant flows.
[02:02] Liam O'Neill: Good question. Redwood uses prefix/KV caching — if your sessions reuse prefixes, cache hits avoid re-computing key/value and reduce initial prefill time. With conversational flows that reuse system few-shot prompts, we've seen 40-70% effective latency reductions on prefill. But if every request is unique, benefit less.
[02:22] Aisha Patel: Our flows have common templates for support intents, so we might get good hit rates. But ramping to 200 concurrent streams, do we need dedicated?
[02:33] Maya Chen: It depends on predictability and data controls. Hosted works well if spikes are modest and you accept multi-tenant routing. Dedicated gives predictable throughput: reserved GPU pools you control, can achieve predictable p95 and concurrency without noisy neighbors. Private (VPC) gives full network isolation but adds ops overhead.
[02:50] Priya Shah: Security: must have SSO (SAML), KMS integration for keys, and SOC2/ISO docs for procurement. Also strict audit logs.
[02:58] Liam O'Neill: We have SAML SSO, KMS integrations, audit logs; we'll attach the security pack. For Private, you can use customer-managed KMS and HSM via our integrations.
[03:08] Marco Ruiz: Network question: for private deployment, do we peer or is there an on-prem option? What about egress?
[03:15] Maya Chen: Both options. VPC peering and on-prem packages are available. Egress patterns vary; we'll share a network requirements doc.
[03:21] Speaker 6: (overlapping) can you, uh, slow down on the acronyms?
[03:25] Maya Chen: Sorry, yes. We'll put an acronym sheet in the doc.
[03:28] [00:03:30] Daniel Kim: For benchmarking, do you have a perf harness? We want to measure p95 initial token (first byte) and p95 steady-state per-token latency, plus tokens/sec per GPU across sequence lengths: 64, 256, 512.
[03:44] Liam O'Neill: Yes, we have a perf-run template. We'll provide configs for sequence lengths and model variants. Our recommended approach: run a 48-hour pilot with a range of concurrency scenarios — steady constant load at expected concurrency, burst scenarios, and cold-start patterns. That surfaces autoscaling and cold cache behavior.
[04:02] Priya Shah: Sounds good. Expected concurrency: average 60 concurrent streams but burstable to 220.
[04:09] Maya Chen: So we should size for 220 burst with autoscaling buffer. For Dedicated you can reserve a minimum and allow burst into shared capacity or scale with buffer policies.
[04:18] [00:04:22] Marco Ruiz: What about cost tradeoffs? We need a TCO estimate for monthly committed vs pay-as-you-go. We also need to understand how continuous batching impacts latency vs cost per token.
[04:33] Maya Chen: We'll send a cost matrix. Generally, Dedicated reduces unit cost at high sustained throughput; Hosted is better for spiky, unpredictable loads. Continuous batching increases throughput and lowers cost, but for strict p95 streaming targets we tune batch windows aggressively to prioritize latency.
[04:50] Daniel Kim: Any pitfalls around quantization and output quality? We can't afford hallucination regressions.
[04:56] Liam O'Neill: Right — quantization affects model fidelity. Redwood Optimize suggests quant profiles per workload. We can run A/B evals on your prompt set during the pilot to detect quality regressions.
[05:07] Priya Shah: Good. For telemetry, we need token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboards in console. Do you expose token counts to billing?
[05:15] Maya Chen: Yes, token-level breakdowns and cost per token are exposed. You can also instrument traces into your own observability tooling for request-level latency and spans.
[05:25] [00:05:30] Marco Ruiz: Are there known cold-starts for model variants? We saw a 700ms spike on cold first requests in our prior vendor tests.
[05:34] Liam O'Neill: Cold starts depend on model size and instance type. For example, 33B on a new container can see multi-second cold starts if model is not resident. We mitigate with warm pools and pinned models on Dedicated. For Hosted we offer warm-up policies and configurable prefetch.
[05:51] Aisha Patel: For the pilot, how do we validate p95? We want to be confident numbers reflect our production traffic shape.
[05:58] Liam O'Neill: Use representative prompt distributions, mixture of seq lengths, and session reuse patterns. We'll help you convert your logs into a loadfile for the perf harness. Also run tests with and without prefix caching enabled to measure delta.
[06:13] [00:06:15] Daniel Kim: Let's talk numbers: you think 11B quantized on Dedicated can achieve initial prefill p95 ~120-160ms and steady-state tokens ~320 tps?
[06:24] Liam O'Neill: That's reasonable for A100/H100 profiles with high cache hit rates and short prefill. For longer builds it will slide down. The 33B might be in 250-400ms range initial. We'll include benchmark baselines.
[06:37] Marco Ruiz: What about concurrency per GPU? How many concurrent streams can a single A100 support for our target?
[06:44] Liam O'Neill: Depends on sequence length and batching. For short seqs (64) I've seen 20-40 concurrent streams per GPU while maintaining p95 requirements; for 256 it's lower, perhaps 8-16. So to hit 220 burst you'd need a pool of ~8-12 GPUs depending on model and sequence distribution. We'll run exact sims in the pilot.
[07:04] [00:07:06] Priya Shah: Can we run a multi-region failover test? We need <100ms added latency for failover region.
[07:15] Maya Chen: Multi-region failover adds network latency. Redwood can route by region and keep warm pools in both regions to reduce failover impact. We'll map expected delta based on regions you pick.
[07:25] Marco Ruiz: For observability, is tracing header-preserving so we can stitch spans?
[07:30] Liam O'Neill: Yes we propagate trace headers and provide tracing hooks in the console and exports.
[07:35] [00:07:38] Priya Shah: Procurement question: how long does contract negotiation take for Dedicated? We have procurement windows next quarter.
[07:44] Maya Chen: For Dedicated, when procurement is engaged, typical negotiation is 4-6 weeks depending on SLAs. Getting security docs early speeds it up.
[07:53] Daniel Kim: OK, pilot specifics — we want a baseline run against Hosted first, then a mirrored Dedicated config. Is that realistic?
[08:01] Liam O'Neill: Yes, we can do Hosted-first to get a baseline, then replicate on Dedicated. Make sure to pin model versions to avoid drift. Also collect sample outputs for quality checks.
[08:12] [00:08:15] Aisha Patel: Any gotchas with session affinity and sticky KV caches?
[08:20] Liam O'Neill: Session affinity helps cache hits but reduces packing efficiency for GPUs. For high concurrency you may trade some cache locality for higher packing. We'll show that tradeoff in the pilot.
[08:33] Marco Ruiz: Network egress costs — do you have guidance on minimizing egress for streaming?
[08:39] Maya Chen: You can compress tokens or use delta encoding for streaming, and run in-region to reduce egress. Private/on-prem helps if egress is a concern. We'll include an egress cost note.
[08:50] [00:08:53] Priya Shah: Okay, let's capture explicit targets for the pilot: aim for p95 time-to-first-token <= 250ms end-to-end, server-gen p95 <= 160ms; steady-state tokens/sec per stream 250-400; support burst to 220 concurrent streams with 95% success under autoscaling.
[09:11] Maya Chen: I'll repeat that: p95 end-to-end <=250ms, server p95 <=160ms, steady-state 250-400 tps per stream, handle 220 concurrent bursts with autoscaling. Is that a fair acceptance criteria?
[09:25] Priya Shah: Yes. Also we want no regressions in hallucination rates beyond 1% for critical intents.
[09:32] Liam O'Neill: We'll run A/B evals and produce a quality report.
[09:36] [00:09:39] Marco Ruiz: For the pilot timeline — can we get a perf harness and sample configs by end of week?
[09:45] Maya Chen: Yes, we aim to send the perf-run template and pricing matrix by 2026-05-29. Liam will prepare harness configs 2026-05-30.
[09:53] Daniel Kim: Network provisioning (VPC peering) might take time on our side. Marco will own that.
[09:58] Marco Ruiz: Yep, I'll provision and share details by 2026-06-01.
[10:04] [00:10:06] Aisha Patel: Quick security note — we require yearly penetration test reports for any vendor. Is that available?
[10:12] Liam O'Neill: We have penetration test summaries and SOC2 Type II; we'll attach those. For Private we can accommodate customer-side pentests during engagement.
[10:22] Maya Chen: Great. Any other blockers?
[10:25] Priya Shah: Budget: we have an initial PO window for Q3. Need high level committed pricing to discuss internally.
[10:33] Maya Chen: We'll provide committed pricing scenarios in the matrix.
[10:36] [00:10:38] Speaker 6: (inaudible) question about token counting for billing.
[10:42] Maya Chen: We bill on tokens and per-inference compute for Dedicated commitments; details in the pricing sheet.
[10:47] Daniel Kim: One last technical: do you support tool-calling / function-calling while streaming? Our assistant uses function calls mid-stream sometimes.
[10:56] Liam O'Neill: Yes, Redwood supports function/tool calling with streaming. There are some subtle latencies when invoking external tools; we'll instrument those paths separately.
[11:06] [00:11:09] Priya Shah: Perfect. Thanks everyone. Let's recap next steps.
[11:12] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood sends perf-run template, pricing matrix, security pack (SOC2/KMS docs) by 2026-05-29. Liam provides harness configs by 2026-05-30. Marco provisions networking by 2026-06-01. Saffron to provide prompt sets and target scenarios by 2026-05-29. Schedule follow-up to review pilot results week of 2026-06-08.
[11:35] Marco Ruiz: Sounds good.
[11:37] Daniel Kim: Thanks, appreciate it.
[11:39] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email and Slack.
[11:44] (call ends)
notes: Perf-run template link: https://redwood.example/perf-template (will be shared privately)
Pricing matrix: hosted vs dedicated vs private - coming 2026-05-29
